ROpening:opening>opener.text: 0 Opening An H-1B filing is an employer’s request to hire a non-US worker in a specialty occupation .
ROpening:opening>opener.pop: A job that needs at least a bachelor’s degree in a specific field, such as engineering or accounting.

ROpening:opening>w4-card.text: It names the job, the worksite, the wage and the company asking to employ the worker. The Department of Labor records the filing even when the worker never arrives, changes employer or is not hired. Why start with companies? The employer is the thread linking the three networks in this story. ! Read the scope carefully These are visa-sponsored filings, not all hiring in America. Unless stated otherwise, the figures below use certified H-1B filings in 2025. One filing is a request, not a guaranteed job. Background A job title tells us what work is requested; a company tells us which jobs, places, and clients are connected by the same hiring system. The links mean shared filings. They say nothing about friendships between workers or companies. The filings leave out workers without H-1B sponsorship, employers that never file, rejected or withdrawn applications, and the wider conditions that shape who gets hired.
